extracted.intended_audience: biomedical researchers (PIs, postdocs) interested in NIH grants, peer review, and research conduct
extracted.subtask_description: Practical commentary and informal guidance about NIH grant review procedures, critique interpretation, grant-writing/resubmission strategies, and good scientific practices for biomedical researchers and prospective PIs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not contact study section chair or members about your application
rubrics_metrics.description: You are absolutely forbidden from contacting the study section chair (or any other member of the study section) regarding your application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: It's pointless and disallowed; SRO is for pre-review issues only. After review, NIH program officer (PO) is the point person for discussing outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use SRO and PO appropriately
rubrics_metrics.description: It is not impermissible to contact the SRO of the study section, but they are only supposed to engage on issues relating to your application that arise prior to review. Once reviewed, your PO becomes the point person for discussing the outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: PO has no more information than you do (the written critiques), though an experienced PO may offer limited interpretive insight. Don't expect study-section members or SRO to help after review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Best resources for interpreting written critiques
rubrics_metrics.description: Your best resource for helping you interpret your written critiques is other PIs who have had grants reviewed, discussed, and scored by that study section, as well as colleagues who are former/current members of the study section (but not serving that cycle).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These individuals can provide insight into biases and preferences of the study section and help you read between the lines. If unavailable, use colleagues with broad study-section experience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not appeal review outcomes
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Author's strong advice: appeals are futile—focus on understanding critiques and revising rather than appealing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Critiques may not state the true reasons your application failed
rubrics_metrics.description: What the critiques 'say' were the key problems with your application aren’t necessarily what really sank it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Seek insider perspectives to identify underlying causes; don’t take written critiques at face value when planning next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: RPG critique template: Overall Impact now requires a paragraph
rubrics_metrics.description: The Overall Impact section now has eliminated the bulleted list and requires a paragraph: 'Write a paragraph summarizing the factors that informed your Overall Impact score.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This change aims to make Overall Impact less cryptic and more informative compared with the prior bulleted format.

rubrics_metrics.name: Five review criteria for Research Project Grants (RPGs)
rubrics_metrics.description: The subsections for the five review criteria (Significance, Innovation, Approach, Investigator, and Environment) incorporate the bulleted list Strengths and Weaknesses format.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each criterion should be addressed with strengths and weaknesses; reviewers use these to inform the Overall Impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact score and percentile definitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact Score is the average final score from 1-9 given to the grant application by all the members of the study section, x10, and rounded to the nearest whole number. The percentile is the percent of applications reviewed by that same study section over the current round and the previous two that had better impact scores than that, and rounded up.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Understanding how scores and percentiles are computed is important for interpreting review outcomes and relative standing within a study section.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study sections vary in scoring behavior (score inflation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Different study sections show dramatic differences in scoring behavior — e.g., proportion scored better than 20 or 30 varies widely between sections.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When evaluating competitiveness, consider study-section-specific scoring norms rather than absolute numbers alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Council/funding-policy effects for Type 1 (new) applications
rubrics_metrics.description: A small number of applications with percentile scores better than the 20th percentile may not be funded; most of these correspond to new (Type 1) applications that are subject to the NIGMS Council’s funding decision guidelines for well-funded laboratories.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Even with a good percentile, program-level funding policies (e.g., discouraging funding of additional new projects for already well-funded labs) can prevent awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: R21s must be developmental/exploratory to be appropriate
rubrics_metrics.description: R21 applications are supposed to be 'Developmental/Exploratory'—if you cut out the only exploratory/developmental part (e.g., in a resubmission) you're left with work that looks like a boring R01 aim.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not remove or neuter the exploratory component when revising an R21; reviewers will ding the application for not being developmental, especially if they reviewed the original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be cautious repurposing an unfunded A1 into a new A0
rubrics_metrics.description: Repurposing an unfunded A1 into a new A0 may be treated as an impermissible resubmission (i.e., disallowed 'resubmissions').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The post solicits experiences — treat this as a policy-sensitive action and verify with program staff before attempting; major changes may still be viewed as resubmission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator and Environment scores reflect perceived independence for early-career applicants
rubrics_metrics.description: Study sections trash grant applications on the Investigator and Environment scoring categories when the PIs are perceived as not being genuinely independent investigators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Institutions guaranteeing resources only if grant awarded may not prevent downgrades; reviewers look for evidence of independence (publication record, resources, plans) and may act to limit 'non-independent' applicants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Postdoctoral training serves both training and selection functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Post-doctoral training is about training but also about selection: identifying the most talented scientists to give a shot at independence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Longer postdocs (beyond 2 years) are often necessary to allow individuals to demonstrate potential; a lack of progress after ~5+ years is reasonable grounds to question PI potential.

rubrics_metrics.name: Starting a new lab requires mentoring less-experienced postdocs
rubrics_metrics.description: When starting your own lab you may have to get off the ground with less talented post-docs with weak English; a key task is enabling these people to fulfill potential and publish.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Effective mentoring and investment in trainees enables lab success until you can attract more accomplished people.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lessons from retractions: run proper controls and avoid cherry-picking
rubrics_metrics.description: Retractions often reveal failures such as inaccurate PCR products, lack of appropriate controls, spontaneous revertants mistaken for complementation, or data cherry-picking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure appropriate controls, reproducible assays, multiple confirmation methods, and transparency; suspicious coincidences (e.g., unconfirmable expression changes) warrant additional scrutiny.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authorship contribution clarity (skepticism about rampant 'equal contribution' claims)
rubrics_metrics.description: Be wary of inflated 'contributed equally' author notes (e.g., multiple co-first authors and co-fourth authors) which can be misleading about actual contributions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Strive for clear, honest attribution of contributions to avoid confusion and gaming of author order.
